note: Verified quotation archive (spec v49 ch.14). Text, attribution and sources exactly as recorded in the spec. Rights must be reviewed before commercial distribution. Add entries here; no code change is needed.

quotes.q: There were many words that you could not stand to hear and finally only the names of places had dignity.
quotes.ctx: The narrator rejects abstract rhetoric (glory, honor, courage, sacrifice) against the concrete names of villages, roads, rivers, regiments and dates.

quotes.q: I hate war as only a soldier who has lived it can, only as one who has seen its brutality, its futility, its stupidity.
quotes.w: Address before the Canadian Club, Ottawa
quotes.ctx: A former supreme allied commander, from lived experience rather than abstraction.

quotes.q: War is a grim, cruel business, a business justified only as a means of sustaining the forces of good against those of evil.
quotes.ctx: War as a grave instrument, not an achievement to celebrate.

quotes.q: Mankind must put an end to war—or war will put an end to mankind.
quotes.w: Address to the United Nations General Assembly
quotes.ctx: A warning about escalation and the shared danger of modern war.

quotes.q: The old Lie: Dulce et decorum est / Pro patria mori.
quotes.rights: public domain in most jurisdictions; check
quotes.ctx: The Latin phrase is an old Roman formulation that Owen calls a lie after depicting the suffering of soldiers.

quotes.q: The United Nations was not created in order to bring us to heaven, but in order to save us from hell.
quotes.w: University of California convocation address, Berkeley (UN record SG/382)
quotes.ctx: Peacebuilding institutions are imperfect tools meant to prevent the worst.

quotes.q: Peace is not merely a distant goal that we seek but a means by which we arrive at that goal.
quotes.w: Where Do We Go from Here: Chaos or Community?
quotes.ctx: Peace is not the final screen after war; the means matter.

quotes.q: Peace cannot be kept by force; it can only be achieved by understanding.
quotes.ctx: Versions circulate with inconsistent wording; verify against a scan of the edition before shipping.

quotes.q: Either Man will abolish war, or war will abolish Man.
quotes.ctx: A stark warning about the existential danger of modern war.

quotes.q: I see neither bravery nor sacrifice in destroying life or property, for offense or defense.
quotes.ctx: Rejects the glorification of destruction as bravery or sacrifice.

quotes.q: The old law of an eye for an eye leaves everybody blind.
quotes.w: Stride Toward Freedom: The Montgomery Story
quotes.ctx: King's wording; do not attribute it to Gandhi.

never.q: War does not determine who is right—only who is left
never.why: attribution to Bertrand Russell is unsupported

never.q: An eye for an eye makes the whole world blind
never.why: exact attribution to Gandhi is disputed; label 'commonly attributed' if ever shown
